backgrounds: Single set: a stylized stop-motion domestic kitchen. Cream/white shaker-style cabinets line the back wall, with a grey stainless range hood over a dark gas stove, a subway-tile backsplash, a grey stone countertop, a grey stone sink basin, and a tall white refrigerator positioned stage-right that stays open for most of the scene. A plain flat light-grey wall fills the right side of frame beside the fridge. No second location or exterior is shown; the whole episode plays out in this one kitchen, shot mostly in a static medium/close framing with the fridge visible in the background or foreground depending on which character is favored.
props: open white refrigerator stocked with visible jars, produce, cheese, and containers
block of yellow cheese (handled/eaten by the black-clad character)
silver stovetop kettle on the counter
second silver kettle further back near the stove
cream ceramic bowl and plate on the counter
range hood and gas stove with black knobs
lighting_notes: Soft, even studio lighting typical of stop-motion tabletop sets, with a warm practical light glowing from inside the open fridge that lightly rims the black character's silhouette. Overall key light is diffuse and neutral (no hard shadows or dramatic contrast), keeping focus on the felted character faces; the flat grey wall on the right is lit slightly cooler/brighter than the warmer cabinetry side.
color_palette: warm tan/brown (female character's felted sweater and skin)
mustard yellow accent (title cards and cheese prop)
visual_complexity_notes: The set itself is moderately detailed (realistic-looking stop-motion kitchen with tactile props like kettles, pots, and stocked fridge shelves), but the camera keeps a shallow depth of field that blurs the background kitchen details, pushing visual focus onto the two felted character faces in the foreground. This is a deliberate choice: a richly dressed single-location set combined with selective focus keeps comedic attention on facial expressions and dialogue rather than the environment.
